_comment: Maps Adobe Camera Raw / Lightroom XMP crs: attributes to darktable module slider actions. 'path' is the darktable Lua gui.action path (module/slider). 'verified' true means confirmed against darktable 5.6.0's own Lua examples/docs; false means best-guess, will be logged if it fails so you can correct it via Preferences > Shortcuts search in darktable, then edit this file. 'scale' converts the ACR numeric value into whatever unit darktable's slider expects (a * value + b). 'enable_module' is the iop path to enable (dt.gui.action(path, 'enable', '', '') if not already on).

entries.note: ACR Exposure2012 is already in EV stops, same unit as darktable exposure slider.

Confirmed working 2026-08-23: dt.gui.action returned a real (non-nan) value and the module landed enabled in the history stack. Exact -100..100 range mapping to velvia's scale not independently verified, just that the path resolves.
Confirmed working 2026-08-23: dt.gui.action returned a real (non-nan) value and the module landed enabled in the history stack.
Internal op name is 'hazeremoval' (confirmed via libhazeremoval.so); base module path fixed 2026-08-23, sub-widget name still unverified.

darktable's 'local contrast' UI module is internally named 'bilat' (there is no liblocalcontrast.so) -- fixed the base module path 2026-08-23, sub-widget name still unverified. Not a 1:1 algorithm match with ACR Clarity regardless.

colorzones_note: HueAdjustment* / SaturationAdjustment* / LuminanceAdjustment* (Red/Orange/Yellow/Green/Aqua/Blue/Purple/Magenta) are handled in code (xmp_to_darktable.py: COLORZONES_GROUPS / colorzones_node_actions), not via this entries table, because each needs a curve-tab switch plus two sequential dt.gui.action calls (force-to-floor, then land-on-target) rather than a single value/set. SOLVED 2026-08-23: the curve-tab widget is named 'channel', not 'page' -- found by reading darktable's actual C source (src/iop/colorzones.c: dt_action_define_iop(self, NULL, N_('channel'), GTK_WIDGET(g->channel_tabs), ...)), which also revealed the three page names are 'lightness', 'chroma', 'hue' (NOT 'saturation', which is why every earlier name-guess against a 'page' widget failed). dt.gui.action('iop/colorzones/channel', <tab>, 'activate', 1.0) switches tabs; confirmed by testing directly that all three tabs share identical calibration: dt.gui.action('iop/colorzones/graph', <channel>, 'down'/'up', speed) is linear, each unit of speed moves the node by 0.01, floor=2.0, neutral=2.5, ceiling=3.0, on every tab.
parametric_note: ParametricShadows/Darks/Lights/Highlights are handled in code (xmp_to_darktable.py: parametric_tone_actions / shadhi_blend_actions, gated by USE_TONEEQUAL_FOR_PARAMETRIC), not via this entries table, because each ACR zone value gets smoothed across all 9 of toneequal's EV-band sliders (or blended into shadhi's 2) rather than a single value/set. BREAKTHROUGH 2026-08-23: toneequal's 'simple' EV sliders (confirmed real dt_bauhaus_slider_from_params bindings, not a curve widget) initially looked dead -- dt.gui.action accepted them but nothing ever landed in history. Root-caused by cloning darktable's source and instrumenting it directly (dt_print probes added to _dev_add_history_item/_dev_auto_save in src/develop/develop.c, rebuilt locally): _dev_auto_save, the function that flushes in-memory history to the database AND the .xmp sidecar, is NOT on an independent timer -- it's checked reactively, only when another history-item event fires, and its elapsed-time condition can't pass until ~20s after darkroom entry (autosave_time is initialized to now+10s, and the check itself needs another +10s past that). A fast script where every action fires in the first few seconds never crosses that threshold on its own. Fixed by adding a trailing 'flush trigger' to apply_xmp_preset.lua: after applying everything, wait ~22s (via darktable.control.dispatch + control.sleep, which must NOT be called directly in the event handler -- that deadlocks the process, confirmed empirically), then nudge any always-present slider (iop/exposure's black level correction, tiny value then back to neutral) to fire one more genuinely-different history event, which flushes the ENTIRE accumulated history at once. Verified by decoding the actual committed op_params bytes for toneequal's -8 EV band and confirming it matched the exact target value. No darktable patch needed -- purely a Lua-side timing fix. This also retroactively explains why HueAdjustment*/etc. via colorzones always worked: that pipeline runs long enough (waiting for the .xmp sidecar to settle) to incidentally cross the 20s mark, while a fast isolated test of a single new action never would have. DISABLED BY DEFAULT anyway (USE_TONEEQUAL_FOR_PARAMETRIC=False): running the real -o pipeline with toneequal's actions included crashed darktable (see stability_note) -- so the safe default merges all 6 ACR values into shadhi's 2 sliders instead, each touched exactly once (touching the same shadhi slider twice in one run also crashed darktable before this was narrowed down).
colorgrade_note: ColorGrade* (colorbalancergb's 4-way wheels: shadow/midtone/highlight/global hue+chroma+luminance) are NOT graphical-only widgets, contrary to an earlier assumption -- reading colorbalancergb.c's gui_init found they're genuine dt_bauhaus_slider_from_params sliders, same as everything else that works in this project. The real paths (found via source, not guessed): sections 'offset'/'lift'/'gain'/'power' (global/shadows/midtones/highlights respectively) each with 'hue'/'chroma'/'luminance' sliders, e.g. iop/colorbalancergb/lift/hue -- confirmed dt.gui.action resolves every one of these 12 paths (real, non-nan values), both with plain value/set and with the up/down nudge trick that made colorzones work. CONFIRMED DEAD END even after discovering and applying the parametric_note timing fix above (which fixed toneequal): re-tested with the trailing flush-trigger in place and verified via byte-level comparison of the actual committed op_params blob that colorbalancergb's blob is still byte-identical before and after touching the 4-way sliders. So this is a genuinely separate, real block from toneequal's, not just timing. The difference from colorzones: colorzones' curve is a custom-drawn graph widget with its own working commit path; colorbalancergb's '4 ways' page is a plain notebook tab of ordinary sliders that are simply not the module's default/master page. The module's actual default page ('master': global saturation/chroma/vibrance/contrast) works fine, which is why ACR's plain Saturation is already mapped there.
whites_blacks_note: Whites2012/Blacks2012 -> filmicrgb's 'white relative exposure'/'black relative exposure' sliders (on its default 'scene' page, not a non-default tab) looked like a strong candidate: genuine dt_bauhaus_slider_from_params sliders, real non-nan dt.gui.action return values. RE-TESTED 2026-08-23 with the parametric_note timing fix in place (trailing flush-trigger, ~22s wait) and still confirmed dead: filmicrgb never appears in the history table at all, on the same proven-reliable image used to confirm toneequal's fix worked. So this is a genuinely separate block from toneequal's, not just timing -- unmapped.
stability_note: darktable 5.6.0 has an intermittent, pre-existing crash (a GTK-internal memory-corruption abort, most likely in its module-group panel re-layout code) triggered by rapid dt.gui.action automation. Confirmed 2026-08-23 NOT to be deterministically tied to any specific action, mapping, module-touched-twice pattern, or activation method after extensive isolation attempts: the exact same, byte-identical action file sometimes ran clean and sometimes crashed against a freshly-restarted darktable. A full restart of darktable (not another kill -9) sometimes clears it temporarily, but the crash can return. This is a darktable/GTK stability issue, not a bug in this project's code. apply-lr-preset.sh retries automatically (up to 3 attempts, see MAX_ATTEMPTS) if darktable crashes before writing the sidecar -- a retry after a crash has consistently succeeded in testing.
unmapped_reason: ColorGrade* -- see colorgrade_note above; a confirmed dead end, not merely unmapped. SplitToning*'s shadow/highlight hue+saturation are graphical color-picker widgets, not plain sliders -- only splittoning's plain 'balance' slider resolved. Whites2012/Blacks2012 -- see whites_blacks_note; filmicrgb was a real candidate, retested with the timing fix, still confirmed dead. Texture has no comparable darktable widget at all.
